resale_co.how_to_apply: No Borough Certificate of Occupancy is needed for a sale. Separately, the Borough requires a Department of Public Works water and sewer House Inspection before closing (see other_items) and a final meter read.
resale_co.contact_title: Superintendent of Public Works (schedules the pre-closing water and sewer House Inspection)

evidence.quote: The Borough does not require a Certificate of Occupancy for the sale of a residential property.
Please note that the Borough does not require a CO for the sale of residential properties.
This inspection may be scheduled by calling the Superintendent of Public Works, Rick Smith 609-737-9440, a minimum of ten business days before the closing date of the sale of your house.
Once you have a closing date email Gabrielle Smith, DPW ( ... ), to schedule a final meter read. Please include the name of your title company in your email.
The fee for the House Inspection and non-quarterly meter read will be charged to the final water/sewer bill.

resale_co.notes: The Borough Home Sale Checklist lists three steps: a DPW House Inspection (609-737-9440), the fire inspection through the NJ DCA portal, and a final meter read. The checklist PDF (July 2024) misspells the DPW email as 'penningotnboro.org'; the web page shows publicworks@penningtonboro.org. The DPW House Inspection is a water and sewer inspection, not a Certificate of Occupancy; its fee is in other_items. Re-checked 2026-10-06: the checklist wording is unchanged, but the site now hides the DPW email address behind Cloudflare email protection (it shows as '[email protected]' in the page text; the link still decodes to publicworks@penningtonboro.org), so the evidence quote now stops short of the address.

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (State is the fire code enforcing agency and issues smoke certificates in Pennington)
authorities.lead_time: More than 10 business days before closing for the lowest fee

fees.label: State fee: Request received 4 to 10 business days before the change of occupant
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received four to 10 business days prior to the change of occupant: $90.00

fees.label: State fee: Request received fewer than 4 business days before the change of occupant
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupant: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply and pay online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety Service Portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'), as the Borough checklist directs. Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email is required and the certificate is emailed once the fee is paid and any required inspection is done. Homes heated only by electricity with no attached garage (no CO alarm needed) should email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official for Pennington in the state directory (Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement)

fire_cert.notes: Pennington Ordinance 2026-3 moved fire code enforcement from the Hopewell Township Fire Commissioners (Fire District No. 1) to the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, pending a Borough fire official for non-life-hazard uses. The July 2026 LEA registry lists the State (S), and the state list of State-enforced towns marks Pennington 'SC' (State issues smoke certificates). The state directory still carries a note 'SSA with Hopewell Twp FD#1'. The DCA fee sentences and the BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov address are in the DCA application page's own instructions (page source). The DCA application title now covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the secondary power source label (no extinguisher). The DCA BFCE page lists Louis Kilmer at (609) 633-6106; the state directory lists (609) 633-6132 for Pennington. Re-checked 2026-10-06: the state fees are now cited from the NJ Register adoption notice (50 N.J.R. 729(a), N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d)) instead of the DCA portal page and the scanned 2017 PDF, because the portal's fee sentence and its BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov instructions sit in page script and cannot be checked automatically (they still read $45 / $90 / $161 in the page source). The Borough's adoption notice confirms Ordinance 2026-3 was finally adopted February 2, 2026. The ordinance itself is a Word file that the checker cannot read.

other_items.label: Water and sewer House Inspection by the Department of Public Works (required before closing)
other_items.detail: Schedule at least ten business days before closing with Superintendent of Public Works Rick Smith, 609-737-9440. Ordinance 2026-19, adopted June 1, 2026 (adoption vote recorded in the June 1, 2026 Council minutes), sets the fee: "House inspections on sale of property: regular fee, $150 $200; fee if less than 10 days' notice, $250 $300." ($150 and $250 struck, $200 and $300 new.) The Home Sale Checklist says the House Inspection fee is charged to the final water/sewer bill, while the older Water/Sewer page still says "There is a fee of $100 that must be either mailed or dropped off at Borough Hall before the inspection."

other_items.label: Water/Sewer page (older House Inspection fee wording)
other_items.detail: Quote: "A water and sewer inspection is required before the closing date of the sale of your house." The same page still lists a $100 fee paid before the inspection, which does not match Ordinance 2026-19.

other_items.label: Final water meter read
other_items.detail: Once there is a closing date, email Gabrielle Smith, DPW (publicworks@penningtonboro.org), with the title company name. The non-quarterly meter read fee is charged to the final water/sewer bill; Ordinance 2026-19 (adopted June 1, 2026) sets "Scheduled: $75 $100; urgent/disputed: $100 $150" ($100 scheduled, $150 urgent).

open_questions: The Water/Sewer page still says the House Inspection fee is $100 paid up front, while Ordinance 2026-19 (adopted June 1, 2026) sets $200 ($300 with less than 10 days' notice) and the checklist says it is added to the final water/sewer bill. Confirm the current amount and how it is paid with DPW (609-737-9440).
